entities.name: Vicelinus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Vicelinus (c. 1086 – December 19, 1154), a pivotal figure in the 12th-century expansion of Latin Christianity, served as the first Bishop of Oldenburg in Holstein from 1149 until his death. Revered as the 'Apostle of Holstein and the Obotrites', his life's work was dedicated to the Christianization of the Polabian Slavs, particularly the Wends and Obotrites, in the regions east of the Elbe River. His missionary efforts were integral to the broader *Drang nach Osten* (Eastward Expansion) of the Holy Roman Empire, transforming the religious and political landscape of what would become northern Germany and contributing to the formation of the Duchy of Saxony's eastern frontier.

Born near Hamelin in Saxony, Vicelinus received his education in Paderborn and later in Laon under Anselm of Laon, a prominent theologian. He commenced his missionary activities around 1126, establishing a monastery of Augustinian canons regular at Faldera (modern Neumünster) in 1127, which served as a crucial base for evangelization among the Holsteiners and the nascent Wendish communities. Despite initial setbacks, including the destruction of his mission by pagan uprisings in 1137, Vicelinus persisted, rebuilding his efforts under the patronage of Henry the Lion and Emperor Lothair III. His strategic approach involved not only preaching but also establishing ecclesiastical infrastructure, ultimately leading to his consecration as Bishop of Oldenburg in 1149 by Archbishop Hartwig I of Bremen.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Vicelinus played a crucial role in the Christianization and Germanization of eastern Holstein, establishing the first lasting bishopric in the region and laying the ecclesiastical groundwork for its integration into the Holy Roman Empire.
